answer: Each identity is assigned one unique quartz shard of a public archive and must remain online to serve it. When the network sends a random echo — a path and a nonce — only the assigned holder can return the correct fragment in time. If two names answer for the same shard, or a shard stays silent across a voyage of checks, those names lose all weight. A farm has to actually host and serve every copy, so idle clones drop to zero influence.
